correctness.rationale: For each prime dividing k+1 the proof correctly separates the zero branch supplied by Guo et al. from the positive case. The all-q Kummer lower bound counts two disjoint carry ranges, and the explicit admissible q=1+p^a s realizes a−floor(log_p b) via a factorial identity and exactly t carries. No other primes divide the gcd by the cited prime-support lemma. The one-prime-power conclusion follows from divisibility of distinct coprime components. A standalone independent arithmetic checker confirms 98 complete gcds, 528238 carry valuations, and 4084 witnesses without treating finite tests as proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating paper studies exactly D(k) but only decides which primes divide it and when it is 1; full-text theorem/lemma examination showed no exact valuation formula or explicit valuation-attaining index. The prime-power-only corollary already follows simply from the published presence criterion, and is not asserted as independent novelty. The leading closely related 2026 fixed-row gcd paper and the OEIS listing do not imply the statement. Multiple targeted mathematical research searches found no equivalent statement. value.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper and OEIS classification identify precisely a natural family of binomial gcds and characterize the unit fiber. The new formula determines the full positive integer gcd for every parameter, including arbitrarily large p-adic exponents, supplies an explicit attaining coefficient, and presents the earlier prime-power-support consequence transparently alongside the stronger exact valuations. This is a motivated structural strengthening of a recently studied invariant, not an arbitrary finite slice or unmotivated computation.
